ledger.x: 1536: Ujiteru died suddenly, Yoshimoto succeeded after the Hanagura Disturbance ('the Genkō faction was eliminated').
1548: the second battle of Azukizaka won against Nobuhide; 'wrested control over the Suruga, Totomi, and Mikawa provinces' in the following decades and 'continued to expand his territory until 1560'.
1561: Matsudaira Motoyasu 'openly ended his allegiance to the Imagawa clan and captured Kaminogō castle'.
By 1565: 'Ieyasu had become the master of all of Mikawa Province'.
1568: Shingen invaded Suruga; in 1567 he and Ieyasu 'came to terms and occupied former Imagawa territory'.
1569: 'secured Suruga after defeating Hōjō Ujimasa's forces'.
1569: Suruga is Takeda land; the Takeda dossier carries the mirror gain.
1568-1569: Ieyasu 'besieged the Horikawa Castle in Tōtōmi' in 1568 and captured it in 1569; 1570 Hamamatsu.

wars.name: Imagawa–Hōjō conflict over Suruga
wars.outcome: 'The Later Hōjō clan invaded into the Suruga province but Yoshimoto defeated the Hōjō's force'; peace with the Hōjō came in 1554 through the marriage of Yoshimoto's son Ujizane.

wars.name: Imagawa advance into Mikawa and Owari
wars.outcome: The first battle of Azukizaka (1542) was lost, the second (1548) won against Nobuhide; in 1554 the Imagawa built Muraki Castle in southeast Owari.

wars.name: Battle of Okehazama
wars.outcome: Yoshimoto was killed on 12 June 1560 by an Oda force of 2,000-3,000 against his 25,000 (page estimates); the Imagawa were greatly weakened.

wars.name: Takeda invasion of Suruga
wars.outcome: Takeda secured Suruga in 1569; the Hōjō intervened and won at Mimasetoge in 1569; Fukazawa fell in 1571.

wars.name: Tokugawa campaign in Tōtōmi
wars.outcome: Horikawa Castle besieged in 1568 and captured in 1569.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, provinces and battles, not borders; Suruga and Tōtōmi are circles and Mikawa is Aichi without Owari.
